content:
priya: FYI I brought up the new HF model (hf/my-gpt-variant) and saw a pretty large sampling delta vs our HF local runs. generation_config.json in the repo explicitly sets temperature=0.2, top_p=0.9, top_k=40, repetition_penalty=1.05 but Redwood runs look like temp=1.0 and no rep penalty. anyone seen this mismatch before?

matt: did you import via the hf->redwood tool or hand-copy the file? sometimes the hf import converts numeric strings oddly. can you paste the generation_config snippet?

priya: pasted the file in case it's useful:
```json
{"temperature": "0.2", "top_p": 0.9, "top_k": "40", "repetition_penalty": "1.05"}
```
I did use the hf import script. note the 3 values are strings in the file (older exporter bug).

matt: ok that's likely it — our parser used to coerce types but there's a fallback that triggers when any field is a string: it abandons the whole set and uses runtime defaults (temp=1.0, top_p=1.0, top_k=0). i filed https://redwood.internal/issue/ML-4523 last month. quick fix: canonicalize types or pass explicit runtime params in the request.

sophie: another gotcha we hit: chat templates can override sampling defaults. if you have a chat_template that contains a sampling override (eg older chat schema had a top_p on the template), the import may prioritize template values over generation_config.json. check the model's chat_template.json too.

zack: also watch tokenizer special tokens. we recently saw a quantized bring-up where the tokenizer prepended an extra BOS token, which shifted rep penalty behavior (it applies to token ids, so misaligned tokenization makes penalized repeats not match). small repro:
```bash
# compare tokenization
python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('hf/my-gpt-variant'); print(t.encode('Hello'))"
# vs redwood runtime tokens logged in console
```

priya: nice. i ran an eval sweep (short completion benchmark) and attached quick numbers: HF baseline perplexity ~18, Redwood imported (no coercion) perplexity ~27, but when I force explicit runtime params in the request it matches HF.

eval-bot: quick-bench: model=hf/my-gpt-variant quant=fp16 run=2025-11-08
- baseline_hf: ppl=18.2
- rw_imported_defaults: ppl=26.9
- rw_request_override(temp=0.2,top_p=0.9,rep=1.05): ppl=18.5

sophie: TL;DR: two probable causes — (1) type coercion fallback when generation_config fields are strings, (2) chat_template or tokenization fallthroughs.

matt: mitigation checklist: 1) canonicalize generation_config.json numeric fields (no quotes), 2) run `rw import --sanitize-genconfig` or update to latest import script, 3) explicitly set sampling params in the inference request if you want immediate parity, 4) verify tokenizer special tokens (bos/eos/pad) match HF tokenizer.

priya: doing that now. will re-run quantized int8 tests after fix and post numbers. thanks all :thumbsup:

zack: if the quantized run still misbehaves ping me and i'll add token-level logging to the runtime so we can inspect rep penalty application.

priya: sweet — follow-up once i have the post-cleanup numbers.
